title: Git facts off the hot path
summary: Decision-ready architecture for single-writer, versioned Git facts: guard every read route against Git spawns, isolate bad cards, persist commit facts, serve slim immutable board generations, and move fact production to the Linux runner host under fenced remote authority.

implementationTasks.title: Guard Git spawns on reads and fix performance budgets
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Guard Git spawns on reads and fix performance budgets

Source: docs/operations/git-facts-architecture/index.html, D1-D6. Implement this slice first. Instrument the common Git process start boundary, not selected endpoints, with an ambient HTTP request scope. In Debug and tests, throw a typed GitProcessOnRequest exception before a read handler starts Git, including detached fallback work that inherits request context. Permit explicit platform mutation commands only outside read scope; audit list, grouped, task detail, Git detail, hygiene and wiki Git routes. Keep production telemetry for violations.

Acceptance: integration tests assert exactly zero Git child starts for cold and warm board and task-detail reads, matching and nonmatching ETags, cache failure, stale snapshot, and concurrent readers. Include a 3,000-card fixture with at least 200 review cards, 2,088 archived cards and duplicate IDs. Add deterministic budget tests for at most 2 KiB average serialized summary per visible card, no full archive payload in board response, and no work triggered by a 304. Record a machine-bound Windows and Linux baseline for p95 warm board latency, payload bytes, index duration, and Git spawns per minute; proposed acceptance targets are p95 250 ms and a 5 s warm ref-change index on that fixture. Mark real timing tests MachineBound and do not make machine timing a routine unit gate. Report any route that still requires a snapshot contract. No product source outside this implementation card's scope is changed by the Dossier task.

implementationTasks.title: Isolate duplicate cards and preserve last good snapshots
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Isolate duplicate cards and preserve last good snapshots

Source: docs/operations/git-facts-architecture/index.html, D4. Repair TestRunService.BuildLookup and GitStateIndexService projection assembly so duplicate task keys, bad sidecars, or one card's Git error produce a typed per-card error and stable deterministic winner rule rather than aborting a repository generation. Use task identity and folder identity explicitly; surface duplicate IDs for repair. Preserve the last good snapshot on repository failure, with age and error reason, and prohibit request-time Git fallback.

Acceptance: reproduce the AGT-3044 duplicate ID fixture and prove the remaining cards publish in one generation; 579 repeated whole-projection failures and fallback spawns cannot recur. Test corrupt sidecar, missing repository, timeout, restart and cross-repository isolation. Existing good cards keep their last values while affected cards show a typed stale/unavailable state. Zero Git spawns on all read routes remains green. Coordinate with the existing 11 October hotfix cards instead of duplicating their changes.

implementationTasks.title: Publish a single-writer Git generation on the task server
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Publish a single-writer Git generation on the task server

Source: docs/operations/git-facts-architecture/index.html, D1-D2. Reconcile AGT-2954's reported 15 unintegrated salvage commits against current develop and the 11 October hotfixes; fold in only nonduplicate reviewed work. Implement one producer per repository with monotonic immutable generations and atomic publish. The key records repository identity, exact relevant head and remote ref object IDs, packed-refs and loose-ref observation stamps, effective config signature, and producer epoch. Ref changes or periodic reconciliation trigger Git work; task events update card task inputs only. Make the request handler a snapshot reader, including task detail.

Acceptance: no-op task-event storm produces zero Git recomputations; one ref change produces one coalesced generation; a missed watcher event is found by bounded reconciliation; a delayed producer cannot overwrite a newer generation. Restart retains the last good generation and typed warming/ready/stale/unavailable states. Instrument run time, consecutive failures and spawns per minute. Keep all current integration correctness tests passing. Document which AGT-2954 commits were reused or superseded.

implementationTasks.title: Persist commit facts and batch integration reachability
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Persist commit facts and batch integration reachability

Source: docs/operations/git-facts-architecture/index.html, D1 and D3. Add a durable content-addressed fact store keyed by repository identity and commit SHA for parents, tree and name-only diff facts. Recompute a card only when its attributed commits, review subject, task input or relevant target ref generation changes. Compute target reachability once per ref movement with a bounded rev-list/merge-base or commit graph traversal and classify all cards from the resulting graph. Do not weaken the existing exact remote containment and gate evidence rules.

Acceptance: restart reuses immutable facts without diff-tree respawns; changing one card sidecar rematerializes that card only; a target fast forward recomputes one graph batch and only affected verdicts. On a 3,000-card fixture with 200+ review cards and 2,088 archived cards, a no-op index pass starts zero Git children and finishes within 500 ms on the reference machine, and a warm ref-change pass finishes within the proposed 5 s budget; report Windows and Linux measurements separately as MachineBound evidence. No card-by-card origin config or merge-base spawn remains.

implementationTasks.title: Serve slim immutable board generations and stable acceptance
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Serve slim immutable board generations and stable acceptance

Source: docs/operations/git-facts-architecture/index.html, D5-D6; AGT-2703 and AGT-3041. Pre-serialize authorized slim card summaries per task/Git/runtime generation, with detail and large review or patch fields fetched on demand. Publish TaskIndexCache filesystem projections ahead of reads too, so an expired or invalidated task snapshot never makes the board request perform or wait for a full scan. Preserve strong ETag/304 coverage for all visible inputs and access scope. Replace BoardReadConcurrencyGate's one serialization slot with immutable generation reads and measured bounded memory. Change completion-claim freshness to bind reviewed subject/result SHA, attribution and containment/verification evidence, so a target ref fast forward preserving containment does not stale Delivered acceptance.

Acceptance: the 235-card fixture uses at most 2 KiB average serialized summary per visible card and at most 512 KiB total grouped body excluding explicit fixed metadata; archive rows are paged or fetched separately. Matching ETag returns 304 with empty body and zero enrichment/serialization. Concurrent readers neither scan task files nor queue behind one response slot nor multiply full-board allocations. A fast forward unrelated to a delivered subject preserves the acceptance; force move or lost containment invalidates it. Zero Git spawns on reads remains green. Add relevant Playwright coverage and light/dark screenshots for changed visible states.

implementationTasks.title: Publish Git facts from a fenced Linux runner
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Publish Git facts from a fenced Linux runner

Source: docs/operations/git-facts-architecture/index.html, D1 and D4; docs/operations/remote-gate-zielbild/index.html; AGT-2737. After remote Task Server authority and remote integration publication prerequisites are accepted, move the per-repository fact producer to the Linux runner host close to the canonical repository. Publish authenticated immutable generations with repository ID, ref object IDs, config signature, producer epoch/fence, generation, checksum and source range. The Task Server validates monotonicity, persists the last good generation and serves it without local Git. The dev seat is an observer. Reconcile after host loss or lost acknowledgement; never let a stale host overwrite a newer generation.

Acceptance: shadow one repository against the task-server producer through 20 comparable ref changes, including normal fast forward, packed-ref change, missed watcher event, host restart, task-server restart, lost publication acknowledgement and stale fence. Match card verdicts and generation sources exactly. With Studio and the Windows task server Git checkout idle, board and detail reads remain available from last good data; visible health shows age, three-failure alarm and the 120-spawn/min catch-up warning. Record CPU, spawn counts and p95 read latency before and after. Do not grant the fact producer ref write authority.

implementationTasks.title: Benchmark Git read engines and repository maintenance
implementationTasks.promptMarkdown:
# Benchmark Git read engines and repository maintenance

Source: docs/operations/git-facts-architecture/index.html, D3. Benchmark bounded CLI, a long-lived git cat-file --batch reader, LibGit2Sharp, and a small gitoxide sidecar for rev-parse, merge-base, diff-tree --name-only and effective config reads on the same Windows and Linux fixtures. Separate cold and warm object cache, process startup, total CPU, memory, p50/p95 latency and correctness. Include packed refs, worktrees, conditional Git config, shallow history, missing objects and concurrent ref movement. Measure core.commitGraph, fetch.writeCommitGraph, scheduled git maintenance, and fsmonitor/untrackedCache only for paths where status is required. Keep the existing platform owned Git writer unchanged.

Acceptance: publish raw commands, repository sizes, host specs and results under the implementation card; select a reader only if it is correct on both platforms and improves end-to-end producer cost without introducing a permanent process leak or deployment fragility. If no option clearly wins, retain bounded CLI plus the persistent commit cache. No request route may call the selected reader directly.
